faq.title: How to Use
faq.desc: Turn your long-form videos into dozens of viral, ready-to-post clips in minutes:
faq.step1_desc: Paste a YouTube URL or select a local video file from your computer.
faq.step2_desc: Enter your OpenAI or Gemini API Key in Settings to power the AI analysis.
faq.step3_desc: Hit 'Generate Viral Clips'. The AI will find the best hooks, create transcripts, and add subtitles automatically.
faq.step4_desc: Not quite right? Use AI Correction or Re-render to tweak aspect ratios and subtitle styles before downloading.
faq.note_desc: Add a Pexels API Key in Settings to instantly spice up your clips with relevant b-roll footage.

help.title: Help & Guide
help.logs_fetch_error: Failed to load logs. Is the backend running?

faqs.a: The app is 100% free and runs locally on your machine. You only need to provide your own API Key (OpenAI/Gemini), which typically costs pennies per usage.

faqs.q: What video sources can I use?
faqs.a: You can paste any public YouTube link (including Shorts) or upload local video files directly from your computer.

faqs.q: The AI picked the wrong highlights. How can I fix this?
faqs.a: Use the 'AI Correction' feature in the History tab. You can give the AI specific instructions like 'Focus only on the SEO tips' and it will regenerate the clip selection.
Once you add a free Pexels API Key in settings, the AI automatically finds and inserts relevant stock footage (B-Roll) based on what's being said, making your clips much more engaging.

faqs.q: Can I resize clips for TikTok, Instagram Reels, or YouTube Shorts?
faqs.a: Absolutely. Go to History and click Re-render on any clip. You can switch aspect ratios (9:16, 4:5, 1:1, 16:9) and change subtitle styles without starting from scratch.

faqs.q: Why does the video rendering take a while?
faqs.a: For maximum privacy, Auto Clipper processes all video rendering (ffmpeg) locally on your computer. The speed depends entirely on your hardware specs.

faqs.q: Can I use my own or a local AI model (Ollama, LM Studio, etc.)?
faqs.a: Yes. In Settings → AI Provider, choose "Custom (OpenAI Compatible)", then click "Set Custom Configuration" and fill in three fields: Base URL (e.g. http://localhost:11434/v1 for Ollama), Model Name (e.g. llama3), and API Key. Leave the API Key empty if your local server doesn't need one. This lets you connect any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — self-hosted Ollama/LM Studio/vLLM or third-party APIs — so you can use free local models without usage limits. Note: transcription still runs locally; the custom model only picks the highlights.

faqs.q: macOS: the backend status stays "Disconnected". How do I fix it?
faqs.a: This affects macOS users who install from the .dmg. The macOS build isn't notarized by Apple yet, so downloading it tags the app and its bundled backend with a quarantine flag, and macOS Gatekeeper blocks the backend from starting — the window opens but the status stays "Disconnected". Fix it once: open the Terminal app and run  xattr -cr "/Applications/Auto Clipper.app"  then reopen Auto Clipper. The status should turn "Connected". Note: right-click → Open alone is often not enough, because it only clears the app shell and not the backend inside it. You only need to do this once per install.

cookies.title: YouTube cookies
cookies.intro: If YouTube asks for verification before a video can be downloaded, upload a cookies.txt file here. The file holds proof of login from your browser.
cookies.warn_title: Use a spare account, not your main one
cookies.warn_body: YouTube can restrict an account whose cookies are used for downloading. Use a separate Google account kept for this.
cookies.guide_title: How to get the cookies.txt file
cookies.step1: In your computer's browser, install the "Get cookies.txt LOCALLY" extension.
cookies.step2: Open youtube.com and log in with the spare account.
cookies.step3: On that YouTube tab, click the extension's icon, choose Export, then upload the file here.
cookies.status_load_failed: The cookies status could not be loaded. Make sure the app is still connected, then try again.
cookies.status_none: No cookies file is stored yet.
cookies.status_ok: The cookies file is stored and still valid.
cookies.logged_out_title: This file is not from a logged-in account
cookies.logged_out_body: These cookies were exported while the browser was not logged in to YouTube, so YouTube will still ask for verification. Log in to YouTube with the spare account, then export and upload again.
cookies.upload_failed: The cookies file could not be uploaded. Try again.
cookies.delete_failed: The cookies file could not be deleted. Try again.
cookies.delete_confirm: Delete the stored cookies file? Videos that ask for verification cannot be downloaded until you upload a new file.
cookies.privacy: The file is stored on this computer and is only used when downloading videos.
cookies.privacy_cloud: The file is stored in the app's data folder (on Google Colab: your Google Drive, folder AutoClipperData/cookies) and is only used when downloading videos.
